::: {#exm-mae-gaussian}
#### Mean absolute error of a Gaussian estimator

Suppose an estimator $\hparam$ has a Gaussian distribution
with mean $\param$ and standard deviation $\sdest$,
so that its estimation error $\erf{\hparam} = \hparam - \param$
has the same distribution as $\sdest Z$,
where $Z$ has a standard Gaussian distribution
with density $\normpdf(z) = (2\pi)^{-1/2} e^{-z^2/2}$.
Then:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\maelr{\hparam}
&= \E{\abs{\sdest Z}}
&& \text{(definition of MAE)}\\
&= \E{\sdest \abs{Z}}
&& \text{($\abs{\sdest Z} = \sdest \abs{Z}$ because $\sdest > 0$)}\\
&= \sdest \E{\abs{Z}}
&& \text{(factor the constant $\sdest$ out of the expectation)}\\
&= \sdest \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \abs{z} \normpdf(z) \, dz
&& \text{(expectation of a function of $Z$)}\\
&= \sdest \cdot 2 \int_{0}^{\infty} \abs{z} \normpdf(z) \, dz
&& \text{($\abs{z}\normpdf(z)$ is symmetric about 0)}\\
&= \sdest \cdot 2 \int_{0}^{\infty} z \normpdf(z) \, dz
&& \text{($\abs{z} = z$ for $z \ge 0$)}\\
&= \sdest \cdot 2 \sb{-\normpdf(z)}_{0}^{\infty}
&& \text{($\normpdf'(z) = -z\normpdf(z)$)}\\
&= \sdest \cdot 2 \paren{\lim_{z \to \infty} \sb{-\normpdf(z)} - \paren{-\normpdf(0)}}
&& \text{(evaluate at the limits)}\\
&= \sdest \cdot 2 \paren{\lim_{z \to \infty} \sb{-\normpdf(z)} + \normpdf(0)}
&& \text{(subtracting a negative is adding)}\\
&= \sdest \cdot 2 \paren{0 + \normpdf(0)}
&& \text{($\normpdf(z) \to 0$ as $z \to \infty$)}\\
&= \sdest \cdot 2 \normpdf(0)
&& \text{(drop the zero term)}\\
&= \sdest \cdot 2 (2\pi)^{-1/2}
&& \text{($\normpdf(0) = (2\pi)^{-1/2}$)}\\
&= \sdest \cdot 2 \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}
&& \text{(write $(2\pi)^{-1/2}$ as $1/\sqrt{2\pi}$)}\\
&= \sdest \cdot \frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}}
&& \text{(multiply)}\\
&= \sdest \cdot \frac{\sqrt{4}}{\sqrt{2\pi}}
&& \text{(write $2$ as $\sqrt{4}$)}\\
&= \sdest \sqrt{4/(2\pi)}
&& \text{(quotient of square roots)}\\
&= \sdest \sqrt{2/\pi}
&& \text{(cancel the common factor 2 in $4/(2\pi)$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

So for an [unbiased](#def-unbiased) Gaussian estimator,
the mean absolute error is about $0.80$ times the standard deviation $\sdest$,
while the [root mean squared error](#def-rmse) is $\sdest$ itself
(@thm-unbiased-props).
:::
